passages.text: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied: “So my anxious thoughts compel me to answer, because of the turmoil within me.
passages.sermon:
Zophar was a Naamathite.
Zophar replied.
Zophar had anxious thoughts.
These thoughts compelled Zophar to answer.
Zophar felt turmoil inside himself.
This turmoil made Zophar speak.
passages.original: וַ֭יַּעַן צֹפַ֥ר הַנַּֽעֲמָתִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ לָ֭כֵן שְׂעִפַּ֣י יְשִׁיב֑וּנִי וּ֝בַעֲב֗וּר ח֣וּשִׁי בִֽי׃

passages.text: I have heard a rebuke that insults me, and my understanding prompts a reply.
passages.sermon:
Zophar the Naamathite speaks.
He hears a rebuke.
The rebuke insults him.
His understanding prompts him to answer.
passages.original: מוּסַ֣ר כְּלִמָּתִ֣י אֶשְׁמָ֑ע וְ֝ר֗וּחַ מִֽבִּינָתִ֥י יַעֲנֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Do you not know that from antiquity, since man was placed on the earth, the triumph of the wicked has been brief and the joy of the godless momentary?
passages.sermon:
Zophar the Naamathite spoke to Job.
Zophar asked Job a question.
Zophar said, "Do you know this truth?"
This truth has existed since ancient times.
God placed mankind on the earth long ago.
Since then, the wicked have not triumphed for long.
The wicked may rejoice, but their joy is brief.
The godless may be happy, but their happiness lasts only a moment.
passages.original: הֲזֹ֣את יָ֭דַעְתָּ מִנִּי־ עַ֑ד מִנִּ֤י שִׂ֖ים אָדָ֣ם עֲלֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃ כִּ֤י רִנְנַ֣ת רְ֭שָׁעִים מִקָּר֑וֹב וְשִׂמְחַ֖ת חָנֵ֣ף עֲדֵי־ רָֽגַע׃

passages.text: Though his arrogance reaches the heavens, and his head touches the clouds, he will perish forever, like his own dung; those who had seen him will ask, ‘Where is he?’
passages.sermon:
The wicked man may become very proud.
His pride may reach up to the heavens.
His head may touch the clouds.
But he will perish forever.
He will disappear like his own dung.
People who saw him before will look for him.
They will say, "Where is he?"
passages.original: אִם־ יַעֲלֶ֣ה לַשָּׁמַ֣יִם שִׂיא֑וֹ וְ֝רֹאשׁ֗וֹ לָעָ֥ב יַגִּֽיעַ׃ כְּֽ֭גֶלֲלוֹ לָנֶ֣צַח יֹאבֵ֑ד רֹ֝אָ֗יו יֹאמְר֥וּ אַיּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He will fly away like a dream, never to be found; he will be chased away like a vision in the night.
passages.sermon:
The wicked man will disappear quickly.
He will vanish like a dream.
No one will find him.
People will drive him away.
He will be chased away like a vision in the night.
passages.original: כַּחֲל֣וֹם יָ֭עוּף וְלֹ֣א יִמְצָא֑וּהוּ וְ֝יֻדַּ֗ד כְּחֶזְי֥וֹן לָֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: The eye that saw him will see him no more, and his place will no longer behold him.
passages.sermon:
A person once saw this man.
That person will not see him again.
His place will not see him anymore.
He will be gone from his home forever.
passages.original: עַ֣יִן שְׁ֭זָפַתּוּ וְלֹ֣א תוֹסִ֑יף וְלֹא־ ע֝֗וֹד תְּשׁוּרֶ֥נּוּ מְקוֹמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: His sons will seek the favor of the poor, for his own hands must return his wealth.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man has sons.
His sons will seek help from the poor.
His own hands must give back his wealth.
He cannot keep what he gained.
He must return what he took.
passages.original: בָּ֭נָיו יְרַצּ֣וּ דַלִּ֑ים וְ֝יָדָ֗יו תָּשֵׁ֥בְנָה אוֹנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie down with him in the dust.
passages.sermon: This man is full of youthful strength in his bones.\r\nHe will die.\r\nHis strength will go with him into the dust.
passages.original: עַ֭צְמוֹתָיו מָלְא֣וּ עֲלוּמוֹ וְ֝עִמּ֗וֹ עַל־ עָפָ֥ר תִּשְׁכָּֽב׃

passages.text: Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he conceals it under his tongue, though he cannot bear to let it go and keeps it in his mouth, yet in his stomach his food sours into the venom of cobras within him.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man finds evil sweet in his mouth.
He hides evil under his tongue.
He does not let evil go.
He keeps evil in his mouth.
He holds evil inside himself.
His food turns sour in his stomach.
The food inside him becomes the venom of cobras.
passages.original: אִם־ תַּמְתִּ֣יק בְּפִ֣יו רָעָ֑ה יַ֝כְחִידֶ֗נָּה תַּ֣חַת לְשׁוֹנֽוֹ׃ יַחְמֹ֣ל עָ֭לֶיהָ וְלֹ֣א יַֽעַזְבֶ֑נָּה וְ֝יִמְנָעֶ֗נָּה בְּת֣וֹךְ חִכּֽוֹ׃ לַ֭חְמוֹ בְּמֵעָ֣יו נֶהְפָּ֑ךְ מְרוֹרַ֖ת פְּתָנִ֣ים בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He swallows wealth but vomits it out; God will force it from his stomach.
passages.sermon:
This man takes in great wealth.
He swallows riches for himself.
He cannot keep them.
He vomits out what he has taken.
God removes the wealth from his stomach.
God forces him to give it up.
He loses what he tried to keep.
passages.original: חַ֣יִל בָּ֭לַע וַיְקִאֶ֑נּוּ מִ֝בִּטְנ֗וֹ יוֹרִשֶׁ֥נּוּ אֵֽל׃

passages.text: He will suck the poison of cobras; the fangs of a viper will kill him.
passages.sermon:
This man chooses evil.
He takes in poison like a cobra’s venom.
He draws this poison into himself.
A viper’s fangs will kill him.
The viper’s bite brings his death.
passages.original: רֹאשׁ־ פְּתָנִ֥ים יִינָ֑ק תַּֽ֝הַרְגֵ֗הוּ לְשׁ֣וֹן אֶפְעֶֽה׃

passages.text: He will not enjoy the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream.
passages.sermon:
The man is wicked.
He will not see streams.
He will not see rivers.
These rivers flow with honey.
These rivers flow with cream.
He will not enjoy them.
passages.original: אַל־ יֵ֥רֶא בִפְלַגּ֑וֹת נַהֲרֵ֥י נַ֝חֲלֵ֗י דְּבַ֣שׁ וְחֶמְאָֽה׃

passages.text: He must return the fruit of his labor without consuming it; he cannot enjoy the profits of his trading.
passages.sermon:
This man is wicked.
He works hard.
He gains wealth.
He must give back what he earned.
He cannot keep what he worked for.
He cannot enjoy his profits.
He cannot rejoice in his trading.
passages.original: מֵשִׁ֣יב יָ֭גָע וְלֹ֣א יִבְלָ֑ע כְּחֵ֥יל תְּ֝מוּרָת֗וֹ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲלֹֽס׃

passages.text: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor; he has seized houses he did not build.
passages.sermon:
The man acted with cruelty.
He oppressed poor people.
He abandoned those in need.
He took houses from others.
He did not build these houses himself.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ רִ֭צַּץ עָזַ֣ב דַּלִּ֑ים בַּ֥יִת גָּ֝זַ֗ל וְלֹ֣א יִבֶנֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Because his appetite is never satisfied, he cannot escape with his treasure.
passages.sermon:
This man is greedy.
He always wants more.
His appetite is never satisfied.
He cannot find peace inside himself.
He cannot escape with his treasure.
He cannot keep what he desires.
passages.original: כִּ֤י׀ לֹא־ יָדַ֣ע שָׁלֵ֣ו בְּבִטְנ֑וֹ בַּ֝חֲמוּד֗וֹ לֹ֣א יְמַלֵּֽט׃

passages.text: Nothing is left for him to consume; thus his prosperity will not endure.
passages.sermon:
This man is wicked.
He has nothing left to eat.
He cannot enjoy any more wealth.
His prosperity will not last.
passages.original: אֵין־ שָׂרִ֥יד לְאָכְל֑וֹ עַל־ כֵּ֝֗ן לֹא־ יָחִ֥יל טוּבֽוֹ׃

passages.text: In the midst of his plenty, he will be distressed; the full force of misery will come upon him.
passages.sermon:
This man is wicked and greedy.
He gathers much wealth.
He feels satisfied and full.
But trouble comes to him.
He becomes distressed.
Every kind of misery reaches him.
His abundance cannot protect him.
Suffering overtakes him even when he has plenty.
passages.original: בִּמְלֹ֣אות שִׂ֭פְקוֹ יֵ֣צֶר ל֑וֹ כָּל־ יַ֖ד עָמֵ֣ל תְּבוֹאֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: When he has filled his stomach, God will vent His fury upon him, raining it down on him as he eats.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes a wicked man.
God is the subject.
God waits until the wicked man fills his stomach.
God then vents His fury on the wicked man.
God rains His anger down on the wicked man as he eats.
passages.original: יְהִ֤י׀ לְמַלֵּ֬א בִטְנ֗וֹ יְֽשַׁלַּח־ בּ֭וֹ חֲר֣וֹן אַפּ֑וֹ וְיַמְטֵ֥ר עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ בִּלְחוּמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow will pierce him.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man tries to escape danger.
He runs from an iron weapon.
He cannot avoid harm.
A bronze-tipped arrow strikes him instead.
passages.original: יִ֭בְרַח מִנֵּ֣שֶׁק בַּרְזֶ֑ל תַּ֝חְלְפֵ֗הוּ קֶ֣שֶׁת נְחוּשָֽׁה׃

passages.text: It is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver. Terrors come over him.
passages.sermon:
A man receives a deadly wound.
Someone pulls a weapon out of his back.
A shining arrowhead comes out from his liver.
He feels great fear.
Terror falls upon him.
passages.original: שָׁלַף֮ וַיֵּצֵ֪א מִגֵּ֫וָ֥ה וּ֭בָרָק מִֽמְּרֹרָת֥וֹ יַהֲלֹ֗ךְ עָלָ֥יו אֵמִֽים׃

passages.text: Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.
passages.sermon:
God punishes the wicked man.
God keeps total darkness for his treasures.
A fire that no one fans will burn him.
This fire will destroy what remains in his tent.
passages.original: כָּל־ חֹשֶׁךְ֮ טָמ֪וּן לִצְפּ֫וּנָ֥יו תְּ֭אָכְלֵהוּ אֵ֣שׁ לֹֽא־ נֻפָּ֑ח יֵ֖רַע שָׂרִ֣יד בְּאָהֳלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The heavens will expose his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
passages.sermon: God will reveal the wicked man’s sin from heaven.\r\nThe earth will stand up against him.
passages.original: יְגַלּ֣וּ שָׁמַ֣יִם עֲוֺנ֑וֹ וְ֝אֶ֗רֶץ מִתְקוֹמָ֘מָ֥ה לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The possessions of his house will be removed, flowing away on the day of God’s wrath.
passages.sermon:
The wicked man owns many possessions in his house.
God becomes angry with the wicked man.
On the day of God's wrath, his possessions will be taken away.
His wealth will flow away like water.
Nothing will remain in his house.
passages.original: יִ֭גֶל יְב֣וּל בֵּית֑וֹ נִ֝גָּר֗וֹת בְּי֣וֹם אַפּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: This is the wicked man’s portion from God, the inheritance God has appointed him.”
passages.sermon:
God gives a portion to every person.
God gives a special portion to the wicked man.
God appoints an inheritance for the wicked man.
God himself decides this inheritance.
This is what the wicked man receives from God.
passages.original: זֶ֤ה׀ חֵֽלֶק־ אָדָ֣ם רָ֭שָׁע מֵאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְנַחֲלַ֖ת אִמְר֣וֹ מֵאֵֽל׃פ
